question: Is there a significant upward trend in world % stocks overexploited?
evidence: Hamed-Rao MK p < 0.001, Sen +0.55 pp/yr [0.50, 0.59]; assessment years only p < 0.001; SAU world p < 0.001
note: No slowdown after 2015: slope change -0.15 pp/yr (p = 0.489), Chow p = 0.892

question: Does global catch cross-correlate with % stocks overexploited at some lag?
evidence: Largest |r| on stationary series: r = -0.23 at lag 4 (Holm p = 1.000); prewhitened min Holm p = 1.000; Granger min Holm p = 1.000; cointegration p = 0.199
note: Catch plateaued since the 1990s while overexploitation kept rising: no short-run or long-run link in this data. Catch is a weak proxy for fishing pressure (caveat 1).

question: Is there a significant worsening trend in SEA (rising % overexploited or falling MTL)?
evidence: SEA % overexploited MK p < 0.001, Sen +7.4 pp/decade; 16/16 countries+EEZs rising after Holm; FAO Area 71 p = 0.074
note: MTL ('fishing down') falls significantly 1990–2019 only in: Philippines; SEA-wide MTL rises, so the worsening shows in stock status rather than trophic level

question: Does SEA catch cross-correlate with mean trophic level at some lag?
evidence: Smallest raw p: Philippines lag 9, r = -0.31 (p = 0.016, Holm within unit p = 0.180); 0 of 66 lag tests significant after Holm
note: Stock status is not used as the response: Sea Around Us derives it from catch (circular)

question: Is the SEA trend in % overexploited significantly worse than the world trend?
evidence: SAU 1990–2019: SEA +0.97 vs world +0.97 pp/yr, difference -0.00 [-0.09, +0.08], p = 0.911; countries worse (Holm): Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand; better: Vietnam
decision: Fail to reject H0 for SEA as a whole; reject for Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand
note: 1950–2019 difference -0.05 pp/yr (p = 0.002). FAO Area 71 vs world +1.03 pp/yr (p = 0.027), but without the 2021 jump p = 0.084. SEA MTL rises 0.0021/yr slower than the world's (p = 0.001)

question: Is catch per unit effort falling (more effort for the same fish)?
evidence: World CPUE -35% 1990–94 → 2013–17 (catch -6%, effort +44%), Sen -1.9%/yr, p < 0.001; SEA -50% (Sen -3.6%/yr, p < 0.001); falling significantly in Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines
note: Not a hypothesis from the plan; supports the depletion explanation for flat catch + rising overexploitation

question: Does world fishing effort cross-correlate with % stocks overexploited at some lag?
evidence: Largest effect r = +0.35 at lag 3 (raw p = 0.026, Holm p = 0.291); SAU min Holm p = 0.266; Granger min Holm p = 0.072; cointegration with FAO p = 0.078
note: Short-run (year-to-year) changes in effort do not line up with changes in stock status; the long-run level link is weak (cointegration p = 0.078, 10% level only). See CPUE for the long-run story.

question: Does SEA fishing effort cross-correlate with % overexploited or mean trophic level at some lag?
evidence: 1 of 132 lag tests significant after Holm within unit: Indonesia Δ MTL lag 0 r = +0.35 (Holm p = 0.043); across all 132 tests min Holm p = 0.517
decision: Weak: reject H0 only for Indonesia Δ MTL at lag 0 (r = +0.35); not significant once all 132 tests are corrected together
note: Stock status can be tested here (effort is independent of SAU's catch-based status). Thailand's effort series stays non-stationary (source breaks), so its lags are unreliable.

question: Does ocean warming correlate with world % stocks overexploited beyond their shared upward trend?
evidence: Levels ρ = +0.86; after removing linear trends ρ = -0.11 with FAO (p = 0.450) but +0.44 with SAU (p < 0.001); cointegration with constant p = 0.051 (FAO), = 0.033 (SAU), with trend p = 0.359 (FAO; ocean heat content = 0.038), jointly with effort p = 0.193; CCF min Holm p = 0.563; Granger min Holm p = 1.000
decision: Fail to reject H0 (shared trend only; no consistent link beyond it)
note: Warming and overexploitation share an upward trend; beyond it the two sources disagree in sign (the SAU series is S-shaped, so a straight-line detrend leaves curvature that matches accelerating warming) and no year-to-year link exists. The data cannot separate warming from other steadily rising drivers.

question: Do changes in SEA sea temperature cross-correlate with % overexploited, mean trophic level or catch?
evidence: SEA SST +0.12 °C/decade (MK p < 0.001); 2 of 198 lag tests significant after Holm within unit and response: SEA Δ % overexploited lag 10 r = +0.44 (Holm p = 0.006); Indonesia Δ MTL lag 4 r = +0.36 (Holm p = 0.032); across all 198 tests min Holm p = 0.110
decision: Weak: 2 isolated lag(s) significant within unit; none across all 198 tests
note: Significant lags sit at the edge of the tested range or in a single country and vanish under the all-test correction, so they are treated as chance findings unless replicated.

question: Do shipping volume, dam building or aquaculture growth track world % stocks overexploited beyond their shared upward trend?
evidence: Levels ρ +0.93 to +1.00; linear-detrended ρ significant after Holm in Container port traffic × SAU (+0.85, quadratic +0.38), Seaborne trade volume × SAU (+0.65, quadratic +0.29), Dams completed (cumulative) × FAO (+0.56, quadratic +0.56), Dams completed (cumulative) × SAU (-0.90, quadratic -0.65); consistent in both sources and both detrends: none; cointegration: Dams completed (cumulative) × FAO c p = 0.191; Dams completed (cumulative) × FAO ct p = 0.062; Dams completed (cumulative) × SAU c p = 0.652; Dams completed (cumulative) × SAU ct p = 0.955; Aquaculture production × FAO c p = 0.175; Aquaculture production × FAO ct p = 0.330; Aquaculture production × SAU c p = 0.554; Aquaculture production × SAU ct p = 0.494; CCF 0 of 74 lag tests significant across all (min Holm p = 0.299)
decision: Fail to reject H0 (shared trend only; no consistent link beyond it)
note: 4 of 4 linear-detrended links either lose significance under a quadratic detrend, have no significant counterpart in the other source, or flip sign between FAO and SAU (dams): they reflect curvature, not co-movement. Shipping starts in 2000 (≤ 22 overlapping years), so its power is low; GDAT completions are a lower bound that thins after ~2005 (database lag).

question: Do changes in SEA port traffic, seaborne trade, liner connectivity, dam building or aquaculture cross-correlate with % overexploited or mean trophic level?
evidence: 2 of 492 lag tests (60 unit × driver × response rows) significant after Holm within row: Thailand Dams completed (cumulative) -> Δ MTL lag 6 r = +0.46; Thailand Dams completed (cumulative) -> Δ MTL lag 7 r = +0.41; across all tests 0 (min Holm p = 0.480); SEA linear-detrended ρ with % overexploited significant after Holm for Dams completed (cumulative) (-0.59, quadratic +0.63), Aquaculture production (+0.65, quadratic +0.22); consistent under both detrends: none
decision: Weak: 2 isolated lag(s) significant within row; none across all 492 tests
note: Shipping overlaps the SAU series for 19 changes only (2001–2019), so only strong links could be detected. Linear-detrended links that flip sign under a quadratic detrend are curvature artefacts.

question: Did % overexploited, mean trophic level or catch in the EEZs facing the Spratly Islands change after China's 2013–2016 island building, relative to other SEA EEZs?
evidence: DiD 2004–2019, event 2014, 4 treated vs 5 control EEZs: % overexploited β = +0.700 (randomization p = 0.913, Holm = 1.000); mean trophic level β = -0.030 (randomization p = 0.476, Holm = 1.000); log catch β = -0.083 (randomization p = 0.587, Holm = 1.000); edge EEZs as treated: % overexploited β = +1.51 (p = 0.701); placebo 2009: β = -8.04 (p = 0.286)
decision: Fail to reject H0 (no post-2014 change specific to Spratly-facing EEZs)
note: Island building is a single dated event; military outposts were built on the same features in 2014–2018, so the two cannot be separated. Vietnam's own reclamation (2022–2025) is after the fisheries data end (2019). Only 9 EEZs → randomization inference (126 assignments) instead of clustered errors.

evidence: H1a: Reject H0; H1b: Fail to reject H0
note: Stage 2 results are reported as exploratory/conditional
